About the Company

Logiqal is on a mission to build the first scaled quantum computer, deploying millions of qubits to tackle the world’s most important problems. Our thesis is that you have to build a full scale machine to learn what the actual hard parts are, just like you have to build a full scale rocket before the first launch. We’re looking for a few visionary scientists and engineers to join our team, to move fast and blow stuff up.

Based in Princeton, NJ our founding physics team has decades of combined research experience at leading academic and industry labs including Princeton, Harvard, Yale, MIT and Google Quantum. Our approach is based on neutral atom qubit technology developed in research labs at Princeton by the founding team. Our scalable systems are composed of manufacturable sub-modules, controlled by state-of-the-art CMOS optoelectronics, and designed around a unique computer architecture.

If you’re excited to build something that’s never existed before at the cutting edge of physics and engineering—together with an awesome team with deep technical expertise—come build with us!

About the role

As a Logiqal Quantum Hardware Intern, you’ll work directly with our physicists and engineers to help build our next‑generation quantum computer. Intern projects are designed to be technically substantial, contributing directly to our optical, mechanical, atomic physics, or software systems.

We welcome applicants from physics, electrical engineering, computer science, optics, mechanical engineering, applied math, and related fields. If you’re curious, driven, and love building hard things, we want to hear from you. You would be a particularly strong fit if you have experience in one or more of:

- Atomic physics, optics, or laser physics

- Experimental data acquisition and analysis

- Programming (Python/C++) and computational physics

- Mechanical engineering

as well as general strengths in:

- Analytical and problem‑solving skills

- Ability to design, build, debug, and iterate quickly

- Working in a fast‑paced, experimental environment

- Curiosity, initiative, and a love of building real hardware

This role is open to current students at the undergraduate, MS or PhD level at US-based institutions. This internship is on‑site at our lab near Princeton, New Jersey. The compensation band for this role is $30-$50/hour, with an additional housing stipend if you are relocating to the Princeton area.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and those received before Nov. 19 are guaranteed full consideration.

FieldAI’s Irvine team is where embodied AI meets real robots, real sensors, and real field deployments. Based in the heart of Southern California’s robotics ecosystem, we build risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that solve the hardest problems in robotics and unlock the full potential of embodied intelligence. If you want your work to ship, get tested on hardware, and improve through real deployments, Irvine is the place. We go beyond typical data-driven approaches or pure transformer-only architectures, combining rigorous engineering with learning systems proven in globally deployed solutions that deliver results today and get better every time our robots run in the field.

Why Join FieldAI?

FieldAI is tackling one of robotics’ hardest problems: deploying robots in unstructured, previously unknown environments. We are solving one of robotics' hardest challenges: reliable deployment outside the lab. Our Field Foundational Models™ raise the bar for perception, planning, localization, and manipulation, with an emphasis on explainability and safety for real-world use.

You will work alongside a world-class team that values creativity, resilience, and bold thinking. We bring a decade-long track record of real-world deployments, strong performance in DARPA challenges, and experience from organizations such as DeepMind, NASA JPL, Boston Dynamics, NVIDIA, Amazon, Tesla Autopilot, Cruise, Zoox, Toyota Research Institute, and SpaceX.

What You'll Do

Depending on your research background and interests, you may work on one or more of the following areas:

- Robot Behavior & Learning: Research methods for learning, adapting, and generating robot behaviors from demonstrations, interaction, experience, and real-world data, enabling robots to perform long-horizon tasks in dynamic and unstructured environments.

- Active Perception & Embodied Reasoning: Develop methods that enable robots to actively reason about what to inspect, where to observe, and what actions to take next based on task objectives, observations, uncertainty, and environmental context.

- Human-Robot Interaction: Develop approaches for intuitive human-robot collaboration, including natural task specification, interactive robot behaviors, human-in-the-loop reasoning, and adaptation to user intent and feedback.

- Embodied AI Models: Investigate and adapt foundation models, including vision-language models, vision-language-action models, and world models, for reasoning, planning, interaction, and decision-making on physical robots.

- Real-Robot Experimentation: Implement and evaluate research algorithms on robotic platforms operating in realistic, unstructured environments, and use deployment data to iteratively improve the underlying methods.

- Research & Publication: Conduct cutting-edge research in embodied AI and robotics, design rigorous experiments and evaluations, and contribute to publications at leading robotics and AI conferences and journals.

What You Bring

- Currently pursuing or recently completed a PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Aerospace, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.

- Strong research foundation in one or more areas such as robot learning, planning and decision-making, embodied AI, perception, active perception, or human-robot interaction.

- Familiarity with state-of-the-art research in embodied AI and robotics.

- Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++.

- Experience with modern machine learning frameworks.

- Experience developing and evaluating algorithms for robotic or embodied systems.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to formulate research questions and design rigorous experiments.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate across research and engineering teams.

What Will Set You Apart

- Hands-on robotics experience, including testing and deploying autonomous systems on physical robots. Experience with ROS or ROS2 and real robotic systems.

- Publications at leading AI and robotics venues such as CoRL, ICRA, IROS, RSS, NeurIPS, CVPR, or similar.

- Research experience in robot behavior and learning, such as imitation learning, reinforcement learning, learning from demonstrations, or learning from interaction and real-world experience.

- Research experience in active perception or active inspection, including task-driven perception, information-gathering behaviors, viewpoint selection, or reasoning under uncertainty.

- Experience in human-robot interaction, language-conditioned robotics, shared autonomy, or interactive robot learningExperience fine-tuning or deploying large multimodal models, particularly vision-language, vision-language-action, open-vocabulary, or related foundation models.

DCI Marketing is reimagining how brands engage with retail customers. We design and deliver immersive environments that bring automotive and consumer brands to life, combining physical fixtures with digital experiences backed by data. Our people are problem-solvers who turn complex challenges into experiences that feel purposeful and built for growth. We're seeking a highly motivated student intern to work in an individual contributor (IC) role for the Data and Analytics team. This role is both hands-on and serves to meet timelines and quality requirements. The candidate will assist with building a functional Analytics Center of Excellence practice in both custom and purchased platform environments.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

- Translate functional and non-functional requirements into effective designs and development specifications
- Responsible for helping transform Data into - > Information -> Knowledge - > Business Decisions
- Responsible for streamlining dataflow pipelines across various programs and products
- Responsible for identifying trends and patterns in data leading to increased effectiveness of digital programs
- Responsible for Data related documentation and visual communications
- Actively seeks to learn and takes guidance from other delivery and operations team members
- Support Snowflake services and warehouse

WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE ROLE:

- Currently pursuing an undergraduate degree in Computer/Software Engineering
- 2+ years of experience in data-related technologies and architecture
- Experience with Snowflake DB (programming knowledge using Snowflake, SnowSight and Snowpipes) is a plus
- Experience in the use of machine learning methods - for example, linear regression, correlation, and statistical modeling
- Experience in writing complex, highly optimized SQL queries
- Experience in managing the Data pipelines
- Google Analytics and Social Media Analytics experience is an advantage
- Prescriptive/predictive analytics experience is an advantage

CHS has an exciting opportunity within our Information Technology division. We are seeking a Data Engineer Intern to join our Data Engineering team for the summer 2027 and gain hands-on experience building scalable, governed, and business-aligned data products across the enterprise.

The ideal candidate is curious, analytical, eager to learn, and interested in data engineering, analytics, or cloud technologies. This internship provides an opportunity to work alongside data engineers, analysts, data scientists, product owners, and business stakeholders while gaining practical experience with modern data engineering tools, development practices, and enterprise data platforms.

Responsibilities

- Work alongside data engineers and business partners to understand business requirements, source systems, and analytics needs.

- Assist with building, testing, and maintaining data pipelines, transformations, data models, and analytics-ready datasets.

- Develop SQL and Python solutions with guidance from experienced engineers.

- Gain hands-on experience with Snowflake, dbt, AWS, Microsoft technologies, and other modern data engineering tools.

- Support the development of governed data products used for reporting, analytics, data science, automation, and business decision-making.

- Participate in testing, documentation, version control, and CI/CD development practices.

- Assist with investigating data quality issues, pipeline failures, and opportunities to improve or automate existing processes.

- Collaborate with data engineers, analysts, data scientists, DevOps teams, architects, and other technology partners.

- Learn and apply enterprise data governance concepts including access controls, naming standards, data quality, and documentation.

- Contribute to team discussions, technical problem-solving, and continuous improvement initiatives.

- Develop an understanding of how data engineering solutions move from business requirements through development and into production.

- Embody a culture of ownership, curiosity, collaboration, continuous improvement, innovation, and learning.

Minimum Qualifications (required)

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Management Information Systems, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field.

Additional Qualifications

- Foundational knowledge of SQL and/or Python through coursework, personal projects, internships, or other hands-on experience.

- Basic understanding of databases, data structures, software development, analytics, or data engineering concepts.

- Coursework or project experience involving SQL, Python, databases, data pipelines, data modeling, analytics, or software development.

- Exposure to cloud technologies such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or similar platforms.

- Exposure to Snowflake, dbt, Git, Azure DevOps, APIs, Power BI, or related technologies.

- Familiarity with version control, software development practices, or CI/CD concepts.

- Experience through academic projects, student organizations, personal projects, or previous internships involving data or software development.

- Interest in modern data engineering, cloud platforms, artificial intelligence, analytics, automation, or enterprise technology.

- Interest in agriculture, energy, supply chain, logistics, trading, finance, gtm, or operations data domains.
